screens.name: Learning inbox

screens.layout: Desktop: left rail (Insights > Learning selected); a top strip of agent level badges; a centre column of ranked cards; the docked 'Talk to VP' panel on the right, aware of this page. Phone: badges collapse into one chip row, cards go full width, and approval buttons stick to the bottom of an opened card.

Centre, Change: a side-by-side diff in shapes for each language variant, with locked sections shown greyed and padlocked. Right, Evidence: the contrasts table, the simulation call player, the gates checklist, the proof plan and the cost. Approval bar sticks to the bottom.

comparison.their_best: Issues with severity, MTTR, calls impacted and categories including Compliance; free default monitors
comparison.vp_better_how: A per-moment hang-up hazard from clause timestamps, with an interval and n, cut by caller state. Engineering-vs-content triage. A health strip that never says 'all good' with nothing watched.

comparison.their_best: Turns failed calls into simulation tests and proposes diffs once a person asks
comparison.vp_better_how: Flagged in code at median call 13-15 for a 90% line, with 0 of 4,000 healthy runs flagged [C]. The card reaches the phone within 15 minutes. Regressions auto-revert and other scripts throttle to 25% (A3, undo) while the client decides.

comparison.their_best: Per-setting diffs a human accepts, tested by simulation; the vendor says it runs 70% of its own simulation testing
comparison.vp_better_how: Propose-probe-compose with an invariant and a domain candidate. Contrasts are measured in code over repeated seeds against a measured noise floor. A shared-assumption probe runs before merging. The library is checked first so rejected ideas are not re-proposed.
comparison.evidence: RET-03/RET-58; LMO s.4 (harness2, arXiv 2610.14224); L6 L11

comparison.their_best: Persona simulations with success conditions and repeat runs; latency expectations per turn
comparison.vp_better_how: Personas carry hidden keys and code scores the outcome; a model never grades its own work. Six Hinglish base personas include the elderly caller with a 2.4 s pause. Synthetic personas are derived from real failure patterns, and multi-call memory tests cover a promise, call-2 language and a call-3 opt-out.
comparison.evidence: elevenlabs dossier (account report s.1, velocity.json); vapi AP-17; L6 L10; docs/harvest/hp-handoffs.md l.36

comparison.their_best: Compliance, pricing and identity sections locked; one human-reviewed edit at a time; branch then merge
comparison.vp_better_how: Locks are enforced as an empty diff on the resolved config, alongside a provenance gate (no new numbers) and a manipulation lint. Approval is a hold-to-confirm bound to the args hash. There is never a bypass mode.
comparison.evidence: SQS-64 (V), SQS-65 (no screen, O); EL-03; VAP-61 (Bypass approvals); L6V item 7 (Bland Tornado)

comparison.their_best: 80/20 or 70/30 splits with a significance flag
comparison.vp_better_how: Pre-registration, a power meter with an ETA, and shadow plus permutation A/A per tenant. Fixed horizon with the verdict hidden until the end. Always-valid tests guard against harm only. Randomisation is per customer and sticky.
comparison.evidence: SQS-65; RET-08; L6V item 4 (52-62% false winners at K=2); L6 L03, L04

comparison.their_best: Staged slice, then a quarter, half, all
comparison.vp_better_how: A 20% safety ramp plus ten auto-stop guardrails, including early hang-up per 10-digit CLI under TRAI reg 21A, crisis handling, disclosure and the Goodhart minutes alarm.

comparison.their_best: Winners promoted by hand and kept forever
comparison.vp_better_how: Expiry at 60 days, drift alarms mark winners stale, and a re-confirm card offers a 10% holdback.
comparison.evidence: L6 s.4.6 (plain Thompson kept the old winner in 56% of runs; discounted 98.5% right)

comparison.vp_better_how: A timeline with labels (proved, fixed before/after, simulated only, no effect, rolled back) and intervals. Point estimates are never summed; a cumulative number appears only with a holdout.

Within-tenant cohorts, plus invariant lessons with support counts drawn from simulations and consented aggregates. Segment priors come only at 10+ opted-in tenants under contract, never as pooled transcripts.
comparison.evidence: L6 s.4.7 (wrong winner for 48-55% of dissimilar tenants); rejected.2026-10-17.cross-tenant-pooling; L6 L33, L34

comparison.their_best: An autonomous test-fix loop; publishing without pausing for approval
comparison.vp_better_how: Autonomy only for risk-lowering actions (revert, throttle, stop). Bandits only at 1,000+ calls a day with held-out read-outs, under outcome or seat pricing.

comparison.their_best: Per-node responsiveness, interruption and STT overrides
comparison.vp_better_how: Measured cut-in tests on millisecond parameters (70-163 calls per arm [C]) with a reply-gap non-inferiority guardrail, Hindi lexicons and per-contact pace presets.
comparison.evidence: retell dossier RAP-18; learning-module-defaults.json turn_taking; open.2026-10-19.turn-taking

comparison.vp_better_how: Shadow A/A and experiments add no calls. Simulation runs about INR 100-200 a cycle [I] inside a visible INR 200 a day budget, with the cost shown on each card. Retell AI QA is USD 0.10/min and Conductor credits USD 0.20.

comparison.their_best: Marketing ahead of docs at Synthflow, SquadStack, Exotel
comparison.vp_better_how: A copy linter in Operator replies, the brief and cards, plus a level badge. 'Learns on its own' is blocked below L4.
comparison.evidence: SYN-81; SQS-74; research/2026-10-20/teardown/SYNTHESIS.md l.364; L6 s.10.4

risks: Real line-level effects may be mostly below 5% relative (TTS vendor choice moved intro hang-ups only 2.4 points over ~99,400 calls [V]), so few slow-lane changes will ever prove. Mitigation: dense metrics, an honest 'under-powered' state, the fast lane for big failures (L6 s.9)

The reference hazard curve and the cut-in ICC are assumed, not measured. Fast-lane thresholds and power numbers may shift; one anonymised dialler export and VP's own per-turn data would settle them (L6 s.10.2)
Clause-aligned hang-up timing may be unavailable on some carriers or BYO paths; the transcript fallback needs 2-5x more calls (L6 s.9)

Simulation validity is unknown: harness2 is untested on dialogue, contrasts share model bias, and failure-derived personas can overfit. The sim-to-live agreement metric must be measured before sims are trusted
Rubber-stamp approvals: managers may tap without reading. Safety therefore lives in the gates, not in the human; the inbox cap limits fatigue
Goodhart under per-minute pricing: moment fixes raise minutes. The proposed minutes credit costs margin; the owner must choose
Novelty effects: a new line starts strong and decays (falsely declared in 82% of Thompson runs, L6 s.4.6). Mitigated by a 7-day minimum and expiry, not eliminated
TRAI reg 21A exposure if exploration raises short calls on 10-digit CLIs. Mitigated by the M08 stop and by preferring 1600/140 series for service calls; counsel question open
Clients may not wire outcomes, leaving only proxies and making outcome tests impossible. Outcome wiring must be part of onboarding
LLM outcome-extraction accuracy is unmeasured; at 90% accuracy it inflates required calls 1.8-2.4x, at 80% 3.6-5.5x (L6 L09, L6V item 8)

Competitors are closing in: ElevenLabs announced proactive proposals and automations (EL-53); Vapi's 'Improve the assistant' Composer flow is flag-gated (VAP-06); Retell Conductor gains autonomy; SquadStack self-serve could open. The statistics layer is copyable within quarters
Statistics vocabulary may confuse clients. Plain-word copy and the comprehension test are the guard
Permutation A/A cannot see arm-dependent writer bugs; only live shadow labels can, so both must run
